claims.text: As-cast HfMoTaTiZr has a density of 10.21 g cm−3.
Introducing 5–10 at.% Al into HfMoTaTiZr will reduce its density.
Introducing 5–10 at.% Si into HfMoTaTiZr will reduce its density.
Introducing 5–10 at.% Al will preserve the room-temperature mechanical properties of HfMoTaTiZr.
Introducing 5–10 at.% Si will preserve the room-temperature mechanical properties of HfMoTaTiZr.
Introducing 5–10 at.% Al will preserve the elevated-temperature mechanical properties of HfMoTaTiZr up to 1000 °C.
Introducing 5–10 at.% Si will preserve the elevated-temperature mechanical properties of HfMoTaTiZr up to 1000 °C.
Al or Si substitutes for heavier elements in the HfMoTaTiZr lattice.
Substitution with Al or Si reduces the alloy's average atomic mass.
The reduced average atomic mass causes a decrease in alloy density.
The Al- or Si-modified alloy maintains high entropy.
Maintaining high entropy preserves strengthening effects and therefore high strength.
Processing at 1800–2000 °C for 1–2 hours is applicable to preparing the proposed alloys.
The proposed property retention applies under various loading conditions.
The hypothesis will be rejected unless density decreases by at least 5% and strength remains at least 90% of the original value at both room temperature and 1000 °C.

contradictions.description: The response presents Al and Si as alternatives, so it does not specify one single intervention as requested.

The intervention says only that Al or Si is alloyed into HfMoTaTiZr, whereas the mediator requires substitution of heavier elements; the identity and amount of the elements being replaced are not specified.
